games.title: Chroma
games.tagline: Red and green make yellow. Yellow and blue make trouble.
games.description: A merge game where the merges follow light rather than arithmetic. Tiles that share no colour combine into their mixture — red and green into yellow, yellow and blue into white — and two whites collapse into a prism that takes a whole row with it. Because mixing is a branching graph rather than a doubling ladder, there is rarely one correct move: cash the yellows in now, or hold the blues for something better. Everyone gets the same tile order each day.
games.author: HexCave
howToPlay: Tap or click a column to drop the tile shown at the top. On a keyboard, keys 1 to 6 pick the column.
Two tiles touching side by side or one above the other merge if they share no colour: red and green become yellow, red and blue become magenta, yellow and blue become white.
Two tiles of the same colour never merge, so a board of nothing but red is a board in trouble.
Two whites side by side collapse into a prism, which clears its entire row.
Every merge drops what is above it, which can set off another merge — chains multiply the score.
Fill every column and the game ends. The daily board gives everyone the same tile order; endless is a fresh sequence every time.
games.goal: Score as much as you can before the grid fills. Chains are where the points are — a merge that triggers another is worth far more than two separate ones.

games.title: Cinder
games.tagline: You are one ember, and you are going out.
games.description: You fall through a burning canopy with only as much life as you have heat, and heat is spent just by existing. Everything green you touch catches and gives some back; catch several in a row and it gives back more. The rain does not care. Steer with momentum, read the wind, and see how far down you get before the light goes out.
games.author: HexCave
controls: Arrow keys or A / D to steer

games.title: Deep Six
games.tagline: Six floors down. You will not survive the first few runs.
games.description: A small turn-based dungeon with permanent death and a long memory. Every run ends, and every run pays out echoes you spend on what you start with next time — a blade, a coat, a lantern that shows you more of the dark. The dungeon is new each run; what you have earned is not.
games.author: HexCave
controls: Arrow keys or WASD to move and attack

games.title: Facet
games.tagline: Three shots at the same board as everyone else.
games.description: A ring of mirrored panels, and one beam of light. You drag from the rim to aim, release, and watch it ricochet — every panel it grazes lights up and stays lit. You get three shots to light all sixteen. Everybody in the world plays the same board on the same day, so a result is worth comparing, and there is an unlimited mode with fresh boards when three shots is not enough for one sitting.
games.author: HexCave
controls: Drag to aim, release to fire
Arrow keys nudge the angle by half a degree
howToPlay: Drag anywhere on the board to aim. The launch point snaps to the nearest point on the rim and a dotted line previews the first bounce.
Release to fire. The beam reflects off panels and the rim until it runs out, lighting every panel it touches.
Panels stay lit between shots, so plan the next shot around what is still dark.
You have three shots on the daily board. Clear it and your streak grows; come back tomorrow for a new one.
Unlimited mode gives you endless fresh boards — clear one to move straight to the next.
games.goal: Light all sixteen panels in three shots. Fewer shots is better; every board here has been proved clearable.

versions.notes: First release. Daily boards proved clearable through September 2027.

games.title: Freight
games.tagline: Draw the lines. The crates keep coming either way.
games.description: Depots appear across the map, each one making a shape and wanting a different one. You have three lines and a limited amount of track: connect the depots, let the trains shuttle, and keep the crates moving. Nothing here needs quick hands — it needs a network that still works when the map has doubled in size. When a depot backs up for too long, the whole thing stops.
games.author: HexCave
controls: Click a line colour, then click depots to route it
Right-click a line to clear it

games.title: Hex Drift
games.tagline: A six-sided tunnel at terminal velocity.
games.description: You are falling down a hexagonal shaft that keeps closing in. Roll the tunnel so the open face lines up before you reach it — and it keeps getting faster. WebGL, sixty frames a second, one very unforgiving corridor.
games.author: HexCave
controls: Arrow keys or A / D to roll

games.title: Kite
games.tagline: No engine. Trade height for speed and hope the canyon agrees.
games.description: A glider, a canyon and a clock. Diving buys speed and spends altitude; thermals give some back if you can find them. The course never changes, so every run is against the last one — your best flight is kept as a ghost and flies it again beside you, which is a more honest opponent than a leaderboard.
games.author: HexCave
controls: A / D or left-right to bank
W / S or up-down to pitch

games.title: Lumen
games.tagline: Take white light apart and put it back where it belongs.
games.description: Eighteen puzzles about light. Bend a beam with mirrors, cut it in two with a splitter, and break it into red, green and blue with a prism — then land exactly the right colour on every receptor. Colours add where they meet, so yellow is red and green arriving together. Every level has been proved solvable, and the game remembers which ones you have cleared and in how many pieces.
games.author: HexCave
controls: Click the tray, then click the grid
Right-click to pick a piece back up

games.title: Neon Snake
games.tagline: Eat the light. Don't eat yourself.
games.description: The arcade classic with a hard edge: the grid speeds up with every pellet, and the walls wrap straight into your own tail. Every fourth pellet drops a gold one worth three points — it expires, so it is always a gamble. Your best run is kept between sessions.
games.author: HexCave

versions.notes: Gold pellets: worth three points, gone in six seconds.

games.title: Orbital
games.tagline: One burn. After that it is just gravity.
games.description: Twelve launches, each with exactly one decision: which way to point and how hard to push. After that the probe belongs to the planets, and the only way to reach the ring is to fall past something heavy at the right distance. The line you aim with is the real trajectory, computed the same way the flight is — so if the preview reaches, the probe reaches.
games.author: HexCave
controls: Hold to charge, release to launch
Arrow keys also aim; R retries

games.title: Prism Breaker
games.tagline: Twelve levels of light, one paddle between them.
games.description: A brick breaker with weight: the ball takes english off the paddle, bricks come in three densities, and every level you clear is remembered so you can pick the run back up where you left it.
games.author: HexCave
controls: Move the mouse, or arrow keys / A-D

games.title: Pulse
games.tagline: Four lanes, three tracks, no forgiveness.
games.description: A rhythm game with its own music. Three tracks were written for it — an arpeggio-driven chase, a slower one in the rain, and something faster than either — and the charts were cut from the same notes you hear, so what falls down the lane is exactly what is playing. Hit early or late and it will tell you which. Your best score and accuracy are kept for each track.
games.author: HexCave
controls: D F J K, or the arrow keys

games.title: Signal Lost
games.tagline: The ping is the only way to see. It is also how they find you.
games.description: You are somewhere inside a dark structure with a sonar and no map. Each ping throws out a ring that paints the walls it touches and flashes anything alive back at you — and every ping tells the things in here exactly where you are. Find the way out, one careful pulse at a time, and go one level deeper.
games.author: HexCave
controls: WASD or arrow keys to move

games.title: Stackwave
games.tagline: Every slab you misjudge, you lose forever.
games.description: Slabs sweep across the tower; drop each one where it overlaps the last. What hangs over the edge is sheared off and falls, so the tower narrows until a single mistake ends it. Land one dead centre and you get the width back.
games.author: HexCave
controls: Space, click or tap to drop
